# Planner — Progress Memory

> **This file is the agent's persistent memory.** The `Planner` agent
> (`.github/agents/planner.agent.md`) MUST read this at session start and update it at session
> end. Keep it accurate and current. Commit it together with the work it describes.

## Mission

Turn each changelog feature (from the Changelog Researcher's backlog) into a concrete,
step-by-step implementation plan for the `llm` VS Code extension. The planner does NOT write
code — only the Coder writes code.

## Active plan — 1.101-9 · Task diagnostic awareness

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — when the agent runs a task, it is aware of errors/warnings from problem matchers; the diagnostic context lets the agent respond to issues as they arise. Image: none. Relevance: keep (capability/context) — agent capability. Gap: the agent has `get_diagnostics` + the 1.100-10 autofix hook (edit-batch diff) but does NOT automatically collect task-specific diagnostics after a `run_command`/task run. Add: after a task/terminal run in agent mode, collect workspace diagnostics (problem-matcher output) and inject them into the agent context.
- **Approach:** Reuse the existing 1.100-10 machinery verbatim, scoped to `run_command` batches instead of edit batches. In the agentic loop (`ChatViewProvider.runStream`), when a tool-call batch contains a `run_command` call: (a) take a **pre-batch workspace-wide diagnostics snapshot** (new `taskDiagnosticsSnapshot()` — same `DiagnosticLike` shape as `autofixSnapshot`, but over `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics()` for ALL files, not a path list); (b) after the batch executes, wait the same 500 ms settle (language server re-reports after a build/task), take the **post snapshot**, and diff with the existing pure `newDiagnostics(before, after)`; (c) if new problems exist, push a **system message** into `this.history` (so the model sees it on the next turn and can react) formatted by a new pure helper `formatTaskDiagnostics` in `ToolExecutor.ts` (header + capped 10-entry list, mirroring `formatNewDiagnostics`), and post an informational `delta` note (`[task diagnostics: N new problems]`). This does NOT consume the `MAX_AUTOFIX_ROUNDS` autofix budget (that budget is for edit-introduced problems; task diagnostics are informational context — the model decides whether to fix). Gated by a new `llm.agent.taskDiagnostics` setting (boolean, default `true`, read as `agentTaskDiagnostics` in `config.ts`). No webview change required (the `delta` message type already exists). No new npm dependencies.
- **Files to touch:** `src/tools/ToolExecutor.ts`, `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `package.json`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/tools/ToolExecutor.ts` (1 file): add `export function formatTaskDiagnostics(command: string, diags: readonly DiagnosticLike[]): string` (pure, no vscode import) — returns `""` when `diags.length === 0`; otherwise a block: `New problems after running "${command}" (${diags.length}):` + one line per diagnostic (first 10) formatted `  <Severity> <file-agnostic line:col> — <message>` using the same severity-name mapping as `formatNewDiagnostics` (`Error`/`Warning`/`Info`/`Hint`), + ` (+N more)` when capped. (No file path in the pure helper — the caller prefixes paths; keeps the helper testable without vscode.) Compiles standalone: one exported pure function.
  - **S-002** — `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts` (1 file): (a) import `formatTaskDiagnostics` from `../tools/ToolExecutor`; (b) new `private taskDiagnosticsSnapshot(): DiagnosticLike[]` — workspace-wide: `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics()` (all-files overload) mapped to `DiagnosticLike[]` (same mapping as `autofixSnapshot`); (c) in the agentic loop, next to the existing `editedPaths`/`before` autofix block (~line 2133): compute `const hasTask = toolCalls.some(c => c.function.name === "run_command")` and `const taskBefore = (settings.agentTaskDiagnostics && hasTask) ? this.taskDiagnosticsSnapshot() : null`; (d) after the existing autofix hook block (~line 2313–2345), add a parallel block: when `taskBefore !== null` → `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500))` (settle), `const taskAfter = this.taskDiagnosticsSnapshot()`, `const fresh = newDiagnostics(taskBefore, taskAfter)`; if `fresh.length > 0` → `const text = formatTaskDiagnostics(<the run_command's command string, parsed from the first run_command call's JSON args, fallback "task">, fresh)`; push `{ role: "system", content: "Task diagnostics: " + text + " Review these problems and fix them if they are caused by the task." }` into `this.history` and post `{ type: "delta", content: "\n\n[task diagnostics: " + fresh.length + " new problems]" }`. Does NOT touch `autoFixRounds`. Compiles standalone: one import, one private method, two small loop edits.
  - **S-003** — `src/config.ts` + `package.json` (2 files): (a) `config.ts`: `Settings` += `agentTaskDiagnostics: boolean`; read `c.get<boolean>("agent.taskDiagnostics", true)` next to the existing `agentAutoFix`/`agentTrackManualEdits` reads (~line 91). (b) `package.json`: add `llm.agent.taskDiagnostics` (boolean, default `true`, description "After the agent runs a task (run_command), automatically collect new problem-matcher diagnostics and inject them into the agent context.") to `contributes.configuration.properties` next to `llm.agent.autoFix`. Compiles standalone: type + field + JSON.
  - **S-004** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new named guards (12): (1) `formatTaskDiagnostics` exported from `ToolExecutor.ts` (static source check); (2) `formatTaskDiagnostics` returns `""` for an empty list (direct import); (3) `formatTaskDiagnostics` formats a 3-entry list with the header `New problems after running` and severity names (direct import); (4) `formatTaskDiagnostics` caps at 10 entries and appends `(+N more)` for 12 entries (direct import); (5) `ChatViewProvider.ts` has `taskDiagnosticsSnapshot` using the all-files `getDiagnostics()` overload (static check); (6) `ChatViewProvider.ts` detects `run_command` in the batch (`hasTask` / `some(c => c.function.name === "run_command")`) (static check); (7) `ChatViewProvider.ts` takes the pre-batch snapshot gated on `settings.agentTaskDiagnostics` (static check); (8) `ChatViewProvider.ts` diffs via `newDiagnostics` after the 500 ms settle and pushes a `system` history message (static check); (9) `ChatViewProvider.ts` posts the `task diagnostics` delta note (static check); (10) the task-diagnostics block does NOT increment `autoFixRounds` (static check: no `autoFixRounds` reference in the task block); (11) `config.ts` reads `agent.taskDiagnostics` (static check); (12) `package.json` has `llm.agent.taskDiagnostics` (static JSON check). Gate **904 → 916** (+12).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** `npm run compile` exit 0; smoke 916/916; in agent mode, a `run_command` batch that introduces new workspace diagnostics (problem-matcher output) gets a system message injected after the batch (after the 500 ms settle) listing the new problems (capped at 10, `+N more`), and a `[task diagnostics: N new problems]` delta note is posted; the model's next turn sees the diagnostics in context and can react; a `run_command` batch with no new diagnostics injects nothing; edit-only batches (no `run_command`) are unaffected by this hook (the 1.100-10 autofix hook is unchanged and keeps its own budget); `llm.agent.taskDiagnostics: false` disables the hook entirely; no new npm dependencies.
- **Risks:** workspace-wide snapshot cost is the same as the existing `#problems`/`get_diagnostics` all-files path (bounded by open files + language-server state); the 500 ms settle is the same heuristic as the autofix hook (a slow language server may miss problems — the model can still call `get_diagnostics` explicitly); task diagnostics are injected as context, not forced autofix rounds (documented: the model decides whether to fix); a batch with BOTH edits and a `run_command` runs both hooks independently (autofix on edited paths + task diagnostics workspace-wide) — the system messages may overlap slightly (acceptable, both are capped).
- **Next item:** (none recorded — confirm with orchestrator).

## Done plan — 1.101-8 · Custom chat modes (Preview)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24 (built + verified PASS, tag `changelog-1.101-8`)
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — define **custom chat modes** via `*.chatprompt.md` files (front matter: `description`, `tools`); select the mode from the chat mode dropdown; each mode has its own instructions and tool set. Image: screenshot of a custom chat mode selected in the Chat view. Relevance: keep (capability/context) — core chat capability. Gap: the extension has Ask/Agent/Edit (1.99-10) but no custom modes.
- **Approach:** A custom mode is a `*.chatprompt.md` file discovered via a new `llm.customModes.locations` glob setting (default `**/*.chatprompt.md`, excluding `node_modules`), mirroring the existing `llm.promptFiles.locations` discovery in `llm.runPrompt` (`src/extension.ts`). The **mode name** is the filename stem (e.g. `review.chatprompt.md` → `review`); the **body** (comments stripped via the existing `stripPromptComments`) is the mode's instructions; front matter `description` (one-line, shown in the dropdown) and `tools` (comma-separated agent-mode tool allow-list) are parsed by a new pure helper in `src/chatmodes.ts` (reuses the `parsePromptFrontMatter` key/value parsing pattern from `src/prompts.ts` but does NOT honor `mode`/`title` — a chatprompt file defines a mode, it is not a runnable prompt). **Selection:** the existing `#mode-select` dropdown gains a separator + one option per discovered mode (value = mode name); selecting one posts `{ type: 'custom_mode', mode: name }` to the host, which stores it in `ToolbarState.customMode` (new optional field, persisted in the toolbar memento like `mode`). Built-in Ask/Agent/Edit are unchanged: `toolbar.mode` stays a `ChatMode` and is the tool-availability base (custom modes run with **agent** tool availability — they are instruction + tool-filter overlays). **Per-request effect** (in `runStream`): when `toolbar.customMode` is set and the mode file is found, (a) its stripped body is appended to the system prompt as `## Mode: <name>\n\n<instructions>` (after the mode addendum, via `composeSystemPrompt`'s existing parts list — passed as an extra part), and (b) its `tools` list feeds the existing `promptTools` filter with precedence **custom mode > `#toolset:` tag > toolbar toolset picker > prompt-file `pendingPromptTools`** (a custom mode with no `tools` front matter applies no filter). The host loads the mode files on activation, on `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, and on a `workspace-did-change`-style refresh each turn (cheap: same `findFiles` + read pattern as `llm.runPrompt`, capped at 50 files / `MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` each) and posts `{ type: 'custom_modes', modes: [{ name, description }] }` to the webview; the webview rebuilds the dropdown options (keeping the current selection when it still exists). A `llm.customModes.enabled` gate (default `true`) disables discovery + the dropdown entries. A `CHATMODE_TEMPLATE` constant (in `src/chatmodes.ts`) is written by a new "New Chat Mode…" entry in the `llm.runPrompt` quick pick? — NO: keep scope minimal, no new command; the template is exported for future use and documented in the setting description.
- **Files to touch:** `src/chatmodes.ts` (new), `src/presets.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `src/chat/webview.ts`, `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, `package.json`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/chatmodes.ts` (1 new file, pure, no `vscode` import): `export interface CustomModeFile { name: string; description?: string; tools?: string[]; instructions: string; path: string }`; `export function parseChatModeFile(content: string, filePath: string): CustomModeFile | null` — parses front matter with the same `---`/`...` delimiter + `key: value` rules as `parsePromptFrontMatter` (only `description` and `tools` honored; `tools` comma-split/trimmed/empties-dropped, empty → `undefined`); `name` = filename stem (strip `.chatprompt.md` suffix, else extension); `instructions` = `stripPromptComments(body).trim()` (imported from `./prompts`); returns `null` when `instructions` is empty (a mode with no body is invalid); `export function chatModeName(filePath: string): string` (pure stem helper, exported for tests); `export const CHATMODE_TEMPLATE: string` (`---\ndescription: One-line description of this mode\ntools: read_file, edit_file\n---\n# My Mode\n\nInstructions the model follows while this mode is selected.\n`). Compiles standalone: new leaf module.
  - **S-002** — `src/presets.ts` + `src/config.ts` (2 files): (a) `presets.ts`: `ToolbarState` += `customMode?: string` (absent/empty = no custom mode); (b) `config.ts`: `Settings` += `customModesEnabled: boolean` + `customModeLocations: string[]`; read `c.get<boolean>("customModes.enabled", true)` and `c.get<string[]>("customModes.locations", ["**/*.chatprompt.md"])` next to the existing `promptFiles` read; the toolbar memento round-trip (where `mode` is normalized via `normalizeChatMode`) also round-trips `customMode` (kept only when a non-empty string). Compiles standalone: type + field additions.
  - **S-003** — `src/chat/webview.ts` (1 file, webview-only): (a) `#mode-select` gains a `<optgroup label="Custom modes" id="custom-mode-group" hidden></optgroup>` after the three built-in options; (b) new host→webview case `custom_modes` — rebuild the optgroup with one `<option value="<name>">` per mode (label = `name` + ` — description` when present); keep the current selection if it still exists, else fall back to `agent`; (c) `modeSelect` change handler: when the selected value is not `ask`/`agent`/`edit`, post `{ type: 'custom_mode', mode: value }` (and do NOT post the built-in `mode` toolbar message for it); built-in values keep the existing `postToolbar` path; (d) toolbar restore (`state.mode` handling at ~line 2249 and the `toolbar` message case at ~line 2457): when `state.customMode` is set and an option with that value exists, select it. Compiles standalone: pure webview string changes.
  - **S-004** — `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts` (1 file): (a) import `parseChatModeFile` from `../chatmodes`; new `private customModes: CustomModeFile[] = []` + `private async loadCustomModes(): Promise<void>` — reads `settings.customModesEnabled` + `settings.customModeLocations`, `vscode.workspace.findFiles(glob, "**/node_modules/**", 50)` per glob (deduped by fsPath, same pattern as `llm.runPrompt`), reads each file (capped at `MAX_PROMPT_CHARS`), `parseChatModeFile` (null → skip), stores the list, posts `{ type: "custom_modes", modes: this.customModes.map(m => ({ name: m.name, description: m.description })) }`; called from `onDidShow`/activation (next to `void this.loadModels()`) and at the top of `runStream` (before request building, so edits to mode files take effect each turn); (b) webview→host switch: new `case "custom_mode"` — validate `msg.mode` is a non-empty string AND matches a loaded mode name (else ignore); store via `this.toolbarStore` (new `setCustomMode(name: string | null)` on the toolbar store, persisted like `mode`); (c) in `runStream`, after the existing toolset-resolution block: if `toolbar.customMode` is set, look up the mode in `this.customModes` — found with `tools` → `promptTools = mode.tools` (highest precedence, overrides tag/picker/prompt-file); found without `tools` → no filter change; not found (file deleted) → post a one-time `{ type: 'error', message: "Custom mode '<name>' no longer exists — using no mode filter." }` and clear `toolbar.customMode`; (d) system prompt: when the mode is found, compute `modeInstructions = "## Mode: " + name + "\n\n" + instructions` and pass it to `composeSystemPrompt` as a new optional 5th part appended after `modeAddendum` (extend the `parts` array; `""`/absent → no change). Compiles standalone: one import, one field, one method, one switch case, two small edits in `runStream`.
  - **S-005** — `package.json` (1 file): add to `contributes.configuration.properties`: `llm.customModes.enabled` (boolean, default `true`, description "Enable custom chat modes defined by *.chatprompt.md files.") and `llm.customModes.locations` (array of strings, default `["**/*.chatprompt.md"]`, description "Glob patterns (workspace-relative) for custom chat mode files (*.chatprompt.md). Front matter: description, tools. The file body is the mode's instructions."). Compiles standalone: JSON only.
  - **S-006** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new named guards (12): (1) `parseChatModeFile` parses a valid file (name from stem, description, tools list, stripped instructions); (2) `parseChatModeFile` returns `null` for an empty/comment-only body; (3) `parseChatModeFile` ignores `mode`/`title` front-matter keys and drops empty `tools` entries; (4) `chatModeName` stem behavior (`review.chatprompt.md` → `review`; `a/b/x.chatprompt.md` → `x`); (5) `CHATMODE_TEMPLATE` contains `description:` and `tools:` front matter; (6) `presets.ts` `ToolbarState` has `customMode` (static check); (7) `config.ts` reads `customModes.enabled` + `customModes.locations` (static check); (8) `webview.ts` has the `custom-mode-group` optgroup + `custom_modes` case + `custom_mode` postMessage (static check); (9) `ChatViewProvider.ts` has `loadCustomModes` + posts `custom_modes` (static check); (10) `ChatViewProvider.ts` handles `case "custom_mode"` with a loaded-mode validation (static check); (11) `ChatViewProvider.ts` applies the mode's `tools` to `promptTools` and appends the `## Mode:` block to the system prompt (static check); (12) `package.json` has both `llm.customModes.*` settings (static JSON check). Gate **892 → 904** (+12).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** `npm run compile` exit 0; smoke 904/904; a `review.chatprompt.md` with `description`/`tools` front matter appears in the Mode dropdown under a "Custom modes" group with its description; selecting it persists across toolbar restores and, on the next send, the system prompt contains a `## Mode: review` block with the file's stripped body and the request's `tools` are restricted to the front-matter list (overriding `#toolset:`/picker/prompt-file filters); a mode file without `tools` applies instructions but no tool filter; deleting the file mid-session posts a one-time error and clears the selection; `llm.customModes.enabled: false` hides the custom entries and applies no mode effect; built-in Ask/Agent/Edit behavior is byte-identical when no custom mode is selected; no new npm dependencies.
- **Risks:** mode names are filename stems — two files with the same stem in different folders collide (first found wins; documented); the per-turn `findFiles` re-scan is the same cost profile as the existing `llm.runPrompt` discovery (bounded, 50 files); a custom mode's `tools` list names unknown tools — the existing `promptTools` filter already tolerates unknown names (it filters the known tool list); the mode body is injected every turn (token cost is the user's choice, same as instructions files); `toolbar.mode` stays `agent`-equivalent for custom modes (tool availability base) — documented in the setting description.
- **Next item:** (none recorded — confirm with orchestrator).

## Done plan — 1.101-7 · Apply edits more efficiently (conditional auto-save/squiggles, aligned keybindings)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24 (built + verified PASS, tag `changelog-1.101-7`)
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — when the agent rewrites a file top-to-bottom, auto-save and squiggles are conditionally disabled; Keep/Undo keybindings aligned (⌘Y/⌘N per change, ⇧⌘Y/⇧⌘N for all). Relevance: keep (capability/context) — edit UX. Gap: the extension applies edits (`write_file`/`edit_file`/`apply_patch` in `ToolExecutor`) but never detects full-file rewrites, never suppresses auto-save/squiggles during them, and has NO keybindings at all (no `keybindings` contribution in `package.json`; keep/undo exist only as webview footer buttons posting `keepChanges`/`undoChanges`/`revertLast`).
- **Approach:** Two orthogonal features. (1) **Conditional auto-save/squiggles suppression on full-file rewrites:** a pure helper `isFullRewrite(oldContent, newContent)` in `src/tools/ToolExecutor.ts` (exported, no vscode import) detects top-to-bottom rewrites: `oldContent === ""` (new file) → false; `newContent === ""` (deletion) → false; otherwise true when the first line AND last line of the old content are absent from the new content (a top-to-bottom rewrite replaces the whole file, so its boundary lines vanish; a targeted edit keeps at least one boundary line). `ToolExecutor` gains `private rewriteSuppressions = new Map<string, { timer: NodeJS.Timeout }>()` + `suppressRewriteEffects(relPath, oldContent, newContent)` (called from `writeFile` and `applyPatchTool` after a successful write, gated by a new `suppressAutoSave: boolean` field set from `settings.agent.suppressAutoSave` in the constructor): when `isFullRewrite` is true → (a) **auto-save**: `vscode.workspace.textDocuments.find(d => d.uri.fsPath === abs)` → if found and dirty, `doc.isDirty = false` (mark clean so the auto-save pipeline has nothing to persist — the agent's on-disk write is the source of truth) and `doc.save()` is NOT called; (b) **squiggles**: `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics(doc.uri)` → if non-empty, post a `vscode.window.setStatusBarMessage`-free lightweight notice via the existing `onToolResult`-style callback is NOT available here — instead the suppression is signaled to the host by the executor storing the path in the map and the host (ChatViewProvider) reading `getRewriteSuppressions()` after each tool batch to post a `rewrite_suppressed` webview message (informational: "auto-save + squiggles suppressed for <file> during rewrite"); a 5 s `unref`'d timer per file clears the map entry (squiggles reappear naturally as the language server re-reports; no editor API exists to hide squiggles without a decoration overlay — documented limitation). `clearChangeSummary()` also clears `rewriteSuppressions`. (2) **Aligned keep/undo keybindings:** register 4 new commands in `package.json` (`llm.keepChanges`, `llm.undoChanges`, `llm.keepLastChange`, `llm.undoLastChange`) + a `keybindings` contribution: `llm.keepLastChange` → `ctrl+y` / `cmd+y` (⌘Y), `llm.undoLastChange` → `ctrl+n` / `cmd+n` (⌘N), `llm.keepChanges` → `shift+ctrl+y` / `shift+cmd+y` (⇧⌘Y), `llm.undoChanges` → `shift+ctrl+n` / `shift+cmd+n` (⇧⌘N), all with `"when": "view == llm.chat"` so they only fire while the chat panel is focused. `extension.ts` registers the 4 commands; each posts the matching webview→host message (`keepChanges`/`undoChanges`/`revertLast` for the last change) via a new `ChatViewProvider.triggerEditAction(action: "keepChanges" | "undoChanges" | "revertLast")` method that calls the same private handlers the webview message switch already calls (`handleKeepAll`, `undoAllChanges`, `revertLastChange`) — no new host logic, just a public entry point.
- **Files to touch:** `src/tools/ToolExecutor.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, `package.json`, `src/extension.ts`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/tools/ToolExecutor.ts` + `src/config.ts` (2 files): (a) `ToolExecutor.ts`: export `isFullRewrite(oldContent: string, newContent: string): boolean` (pure, per the rules above; both empty → false); add `private suppressAutoSave: boolean` field (constructor param, default `true`); add `private rewriteSuppressions = new Map<string, { timer: NodeJS.Timeout }>()`; add `public getRewriteSuppressions(): string[]` (returns current keys); add `private suppressRewriteEffects(relPath: string, oldContent: string, newContent: string, abs: string): void` (gated on `this.suppressAutoSave && isFullRewrite(...)`; auto-save suppression via `textDocuments.find` + `isDirty = false`; 5 s `unref`'d timer to clear the map entry; replaces any existing timer for the same path); call it from `writeFile` (after `fs.promises.writeFile` succeeds, before `recordChange`) and from `applyPatchTool` (after a successful patch write); `clearChangeSummary()` also clears `rewriteSuppressions` (clear all timers). (b) `config.ts`: `Settings` interface += `agentSuppressAutoSave: boolean`; read `c.get<boolean>("agent.suppressAutoSave", true)` next to the existing `agentAutoFix`/`agentTrackManualEdits` reads. Compiles standalone: pure helper + new private members + one constructor param with a default; `config.ts` adds one field.
  - **S-002** — `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts` (1 file): (a) pass `settings.agentSuppressAutoSave` into the `ToolExecutor` constructor (find the existing construction site); (b) after each tool batch in the agentic loop (next to the existing `autofixSnapshot`/`newDiagnostics` hook at ~line 2164), read `this.toolExecutor.getRewriteSuppressions()`; if non-empty, post `{ type: "rewrite_suppressed", files: string[] }` to the webview (informational only — the webview may render a small note in the change footer; no webview change required in this slice, the message is safely ignored by the existing switch's `default` case); (c) add `public triggerEditAction(action: "keepChanges" | "undoChanges" | "revertLast"): void` — dispatches to the existing `handleKeepAll()` / `undoAllChanges()` / `revertLastChange()` (same methods the webview message switch calls); no new logic. Compiles standalone: one constructor arg, one postMessage, one public method.
  - **S-003** — `package.json` + `src/extension.ts` (2 files): (a) `package.json`: add 4 commands to `contributes.commands` — `llm.keepChanges` ("LLM: Keep All Changes"), `llm.undoChanges` ("LLM: Undo All Changes"), `llm.keepLastChange` ("LLM: Keep Last Change"), `llm.undoLastChange` ("LLM: Undo Last Change"); add a new `contributes.keybindings` array: `{ "command": "llm.keepLastChange", "key": "ctrl+y", "mac": "cmd+y", "when": "view == llm.chat" }`, `{ "command": "llm.undoLastChange", "key": "ctrl+n", "mac": "cmd+n", "when": "view == llm.chat" }`, `{ "command": "llm.keepChanges", "key": "shift+ctrl+y", "mac": "shift+cmd+y", "when": "view == llm.chat" }`, `{ "command": "llm.undoChanges", "key": "shift+ctrl+n", "mac": "shift+cmd+n", "when": "view == llm.chat" }`; add `llm.agent.suppressAutoSave` (boolean, default `true`, description "Suppress auto-save and squiggles while the agent rewrites a file top-to-bottom.") to `contributes.configuration.properties`. (b) `extension.ts`: register the 4 commands via `vscode.commands.registerCommand`, each calling `chatViewProvider.triggerEditAction(...)` (the provider instance is already created in `activate`); add the 4 command disposables to the existing `context.subscriptions`. Compiles standalone: JSON contributions + 4 `registerCommand` calls using the new public method from S-002.
  - **S-004** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new named guards (12): (1) `isFullRewrite` exported from `ToolExecutor.ts` (static source check); (2) `isFullRewrite` behavior via a direct import in the smoke test (new file → false; deletion → false; both empty → false; first+last line replaced → true; only middle changed → false); (3) `config.ts` reads `agent.suppressAutoSave` (static check); (4) `ToolExecutor` constructor accepts `suppressAutoSave` (static check); (5) `writeFile` calls `suppressRewriteEffects` (static check); (6) `applyPatchTool` calls `suppressRewriteEffects` (static check); (7) `clearChangeSummary` clears `rewriteSuppressions` (static check); (8) `ChatViewProvider` passes `agentSuppressAutoSave` to the `ToolExecutor` constructor (static check); (9) `ChatViewProvider` posts `rewrite_suppressed` (static check); (10) `triggerEditAction` defined and dispatches to `handleKeepAll`/`undoAllChanges`/`revertLastChange` (static check); (11) `package.json` has all 4 keybindings with the correct keys (`ctrl+y`/`cmd+y`, `ctrl+n`/`cmd+n`, `shift+ctrl+y`/`shift+cmd+y`, `shift+ctrl+n`/`shift+cmd+n`) and `when: view == llm.chat` (static JSON check); (12) `package.json` has `llm.agent.suppressAutoSave` setting + all 4 new commands (static JSON check). Gate **880 → 892** (+12).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** `npm run compile` exit 0; smoke 892/892; `isFullRewrite` correctly classifies full rewrites vs targeted edits (verified by the smoke test's direct import); a `write_file` that replaces a file top-to-bottom (first + last line changed) triggers `suppressRewriteEffects` (open dirty document marked clean, path tracked in `rewriteSuppressions`, cleared after 5 s); a targeted `edit_file` does NOT trigger suppression; the host posts `rewrite_suppressed` with the affected file paths after a tool batch containing a full rewrite; the 4 keybindings (⌘Y/⌘N/⇧⌘Y/⇧⌘N) are registered and fire only when `view == llm.chat`; pressing ⌘Y keeps the last change, ⌘N undoes the last change, ⇧⌘Y keeps all, ⇧⌘N undos all (same behavior as the webview footer buttons); `llm.agent.suppressAutoSave: false` disables the suppression entirely; no new npm dependencies; all existing keep/undo/revert behavior unchanged.

## Done plan — 1.101-6 · Chat UX improvements (distinct user messages, visible undo, navigable attachments)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24 (built + verified PASS, tag `changelog-1.101-6`)
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — user messages visually distinct from AI responses; undoing a request is visible (hover X button or ⌘Backspace); attachments from the input box are more navigable. Relevance: keep (capability/context) — chat UX. Gap: webview renders messages but per-request undo is not implemented; user styling is minimal; attachment strip is a bare thumbnail row.
- **Approach:** Three orthogonal UX features, all in the single webview + host pair. (1) **Distinct user messages:** strengthen the existing `.message.user` styling (accent left border + bolder label) and give every user message a stable `data-idx` (its index in the host `history` array at render time) so the webview can address it for undo. (2) **Visible undo:** a hover `×` button (`.msg-undo`, same pattern as the existing `.copy-btn` on assistant messages) on every user message posts `{ type: 'undo_request', index }` to the host; the host truncates `this.history` to `index` (drops that user turn AND all following turns — "undo a request and all following") and posts `{ type: 'undo_done', messages, conversations, activeId }`; the webview re-renders the message list from `messages` (reusing the existing `restore` render path). ⌘Backspace (and Ctrl+Backspace) in the webview posts the same `undo_request` with the LAST user message's index. No-op when streaming or when there is no user message to undo. (3) **Navigable attachments:** the pending-image strip (`#attach-strip`) becomes horizontally scrollable with a count label; the attach button shows a pending-count badge; clicking a pending thumbnail opens a full-size lightbox preview (click backdrop to close); clicking a sent message image (`.msg-img`) opens the same lightbox.
- **Files to touch:** `src/chat/webview.ts`, `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/chat/webview.ts` (1 file, webview-only, no host changes): (a) CSS: `.message.user .content` gains `border-left: 2px solid var(--focus)` (keep existing `--user-bg` background); `.message.user .role` gains `color: var(--fg)`; new `.msg-undo` rule cloned from `.copy-btn` (opacity 0 → 1 on `.message.user:hover`); `#attach-strip` gains `overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%` + `::-webkit-scrollbar` thin styling; new `.attach-count` (11px muted label) and `.attach-badge` (small rounded count chip on `#attach`); new `#lightbox` (fixed, full-viewport, `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` backdrop, centered `img` max 90vw/90vh, `cursor: zoom-out`). (b) `window.addUserMessage(text, images, idx)` — new optional 3rd param; sets `el.dataset.idx = String(idx ?? '')`; appends a `<button class="msg-undo" title="Undo this request and everything after it">×</button>` inside the `.role` div (role div becomes flex like assistant's); click handler posts `{ type: 'undo_request', index: Number(el.dataset.idx) }` when `idx` is a valid number and `!streaming`. (c) `renderAttachStrip()` — prepend a `.attach-count` span (`N pending`) when `pendingImages.length > 0`; update `#attach` badge text/visibility; each thumbnail `im` gets `cursor: zoom-in` + click → `openLightbox(img.dataUrl)`. (d) New `openLightbox(dataUrl)` / `closeLightbox()` — create/reuse a single `#lightbox` element with an `<img>`; backdrop click or `Esc` closes. (e) In the `restore` render loop, pass the user message's array index as `idx` to `addUserMessage`. (f) `keydown` listener on `document`: `e.key === 'Backspace' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)` → `e.preventDefault()`, find the last `.message.user` with a numeric `data-idx`, post `{ type: 'undo_request', index }` (only when `!streaming`). (g) `.msg-img` (sent message images) get `cursor: zoom-in` + click → `openLightbox`. Compiles standalone: pure webview string changes, no TS API surface change.
  - **S-002** — `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts` (1 file): (a) `WebviewToHostMessage` handling: new `case "undo_request"` in the webview→host switch — read `index` (integer 0 ≤ index < history.length, else ignore); if `this.abortController` is active → post `{ type: 'error', message: 'Stop the running request first.' }` and return; else `this.history = this.history.slice(0, index)`; `this.preRunHistory = null` (stale checkpoint after truncation); `this.pushHistory()` (existing method posts `restore` with `messages` + `conversations` + `activeId` — the webview's existing `restore` case re-renders everything, so no new host→webview message type is needed); post `{ type: 'undo_done' }` as a lightweight confirmation (webview may ignore it). (b) Guard: undo while a conversation is persisted → the existing `pushHistory`/persist path already saves the truncated history. Compiles standalone: only adds a switch case + uses existing `pushHistory`.
  - **S-003** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new named guards (static source checks on `src/chat/webview.ts` + `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, matching the established pattern for webview items): (1) `webview.ts` contains `.msg-undo` CSS + `undo_request` postMessage; (2) `addUserMessage` signature includes `idx` and sets `data-idx`; (3) `undo_request` case exists in `ChatViewProvider.ts` and truncates via `this.history.slice(0, index)`; (4) undo guard: `abortController` check present before truncation; (5) ⌘Backspace handler present (`Backspace` + `metaKey || ctrlKey` + `preventDefault`); (6) `#attach-strip` CSS has `overflow-x: auto`; (7) `.attach-count` and `.attach-badge` present; (8) `openLightbox`/`closeLightbox` defined and wired to both pending thumbnails and `.msg-img`; (9) `restore` render loop passes the index to `addUserMessage`; (10) `undo_request` with out-of-range index is a no-op (source check: bounds check `index < this.history.length`). Gate **870 → 880** (+10).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** `npm run compile` exit 0; smoke 880/880; user messages render with the accent left border + full-strength "You" label and a hover `×` undo button; clicking the `×` (or ⌘Backspace) truncates the host history to before that user turn (the turn and all following turns are gone from both the panel and the persisted conversation); undo is a no-op while a request is streaming (error posted) and when no user message exists; the pending-attachment strip scrolls horizontally, shows a count label and a badge on the attach button, and clicking any thumbnail (pending or sent) opens a full-size lightbox that closes on backdrop click or Esc; no new npm dependencies; assistant-message rendering, retry, and all existing webview behavior unchanged.
- **Risks:** `data-idx` is positional — after a host-side truncation the webview is fully re-rendered via `restore`, so indices stay consistent (no incremental DOM patching); ⌘Backspace is intercepted only in the webview (no VS Code command registered — keeps scope minimal and matches "visible in the chat"); undoing drops the `preRunHistory` checkpoint (documented: file-change undo is tied to the last run, which no longer exists after the request is undone); lightbox is a single shared element (no stacking of multiple previews).

## Done plan — 1.101-5 · MCP development mode (VS Code 1.101)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24 (built + verified PASS, tag `changelog-1.101-5`)
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — add a `dev` key to the MCP server config: `watch` (file glob to restart the server on change) and `debug` (attach a debugger; Node.js and Python). Relevance: keep (capability/context) — MCP dev UX. Gap: no dev mode. Extend: parse `dev.watch` glob, watch for changes, restart the server process; `dev.debug` launches with `--inspect` (node) or `debugpy` (python).
- **Approach:** Two orthogonal, minimal features, both stdio-only (HTTP servers have no process to watch/debug — `dev` is ignored for `url` servers). (1) **`dev.debug`** is pure spawn-arg rewriting: a pure helper `mcpDebugArgs(command, args, debug)` in `src/mcp.ts` returns the args to spawn with — Node runtime (`node`/`nodejs` basename) → insert `--inspect` as the first arg after the command; Python runtime (`python`/`python2`/`python3` basename) → prepend `-m debugpy --listen 5678` before the existing args; unknown runtime → args unchanged. `McpManager.ensureStarted` computes `cfg.dev?.debug ? mcpDebugArgs(...) : cfg.args` and passes the result via a shallow-copied config to `new McpClient(...)` — `McpClient` itself is untouched (it already spawns `config.command` with `config.args`). No VS Code Debug API: "attach" means the server listens on the inspect port; the user attaches externally. (2) **`dev.watch`** is a directory-level `fs.watch` (no `chokidar`): a pure helper `mcpWatchTarget(glob)` in `src/mcp.ts` returns `{ dir, match }` where `dir` is the longest literal prefix of the glob before the first wildcard (relative globs resolve against `process.cwd()`; empty prefix → `.`) and `match` is a RegExp built from the glob (`**/` → `.*`, `*` → `[^/]*`, `?` → `[^/]`, everything else escaped; anchored full-string match against the changed file's path relative to `dir`). `McpManager` owns the watcher lifecycle: `private devWatchers = new Map<string, { watcher: FSWatcher; timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined }>()`; after a successful `ensureStarted` (only when `cfg.dev?.watch` is a non-empty string AND the server is stdio), `startDevWatch(name)` calls `fs.watch(dir, { persistent: false })` and on each event (debounced 500 ms, timer `unref`'d) checks `match.test(path)` and, on a hit, calls the existing `this.refresh(name)` (close + restart — never throws, records status). `setServers` stops the watcher for removed servers; `dispose()` stops all watchers and clears the map. Watcher failures (bad dir, EACCES) are swallowed with a `notify` message — dev mode must never break server startup.
- **Files to touch:** `src/mcp.ts`, `src/mcpManager.ts`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/mcp.ts` (1 file, pure types + helpers, no `vscode` import): `McpDevConfig` interface (`watch?: string; debug?: boolean`); `McpServerConfig` += `dev?: McpDevConfig`; `parseMcpServers` — coerce `entry.dev` (plain object only; `watch` kept only when a non-empty string; `debug` kept only when a boolean; if neither survives, `dev` stays `undefined`); `mcpWatchTarget(glob: string): { dir: string; match: RegExp }` (pure, per the glob rules above; throws `invalid watch glob` on empty/whitespace input); `mcpDebugArgs(command: string, args: string[], debug: boolean): string[]` (pure; `debug` false/absent → `args` unchanged; Node/Python rules above; returns a NEW array, never mutates input).
  - **S-002** — `src/mcpManager.ts` (1 file): import `fs` (`watch`, `FSWatcher`) + `mcpDebugArgs`, `mcpWatchTarget` from `./mcp`; `McpManager` += `private devWatchers = new Map<string, { watcher: FSWatcher; timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined }>()`; `ensureStarted` — when constructing a stdio client, compute `const spawnArgs = cfg.dev?.debug ? mcpDebugArgs(cfg.command!, cfg.args ?? [], true) : cfg.args` and pass `{ ...cfg, args: spawnArgs }` to `new McpClient(...)`; after a successful start, if `cfg.dev?.watch` is set and the server is stdio → `this.startDevWatch(name, cfg.dev.watch)`; `private startDevWatch(name, glob)` — try `mcpWatchTarget(glob)` (catch → `notify` + return), `fs.watch(dir, { persistent: false })`; on event: 500 ms debounce (clear + reset timer, `unref`'d), then if `match.test(eventPath)` → `void this.refresh(name)`; store `{ watcher, timer }` in `devWatchers`; watcher `error` event → `notify` + `stopDevWatch(name)`; `private stopDevWatch(name)` — clear timer, `watcher.close()`, delete map entry (idempotent); `setServers` — for each removed server also call `stopDevWatch(name)`; `dispose()` — `stopDevWatch` for every entry + clear the map.
  - **S-003** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new assertions — `mcpWatchTarget` (literal dir extraction: `./src/**/*.py` → dir `./src`, `**/*.js` → dir `.`; regex behavior: `**/*.py` matches `a/b/c.py` and `c.py` but not `c.ts`; `*` does not cross `/`; empty glob throws); `mcpDebugArgs` (node + `--inspect` inserted first; python3 → `-m debugpy --listen 5678` prepended before existing args; unknown command → unchanged; `debug: false` → unchanged; input array not mutated); `parseMcpServers` dev coercion (valid `dev` kept; `dev.watch` non-string dropped; `dev.debug` non-boolean dropped; all-invalid `dev` → `undefined`; `dev` on a `url` server still parsed but harmless); `McpManager` dev wiring via a fake stdio server (spawn a `node -e` echo-MCP stub): `dev.debug: true` → spawned process args include `--inspect` (assert via the stub printing its `process.argv` on stderr, or via a config-level static source check that `ensureStarted` passes the rewritten args); `dev.watch` → `fs.watch` invoked on the resolved dir (stub `fs.watch` in the smoke test to capture the dir + simulate an event → assert `refresh`-equivalent restart happened: server status returns to `running` with a fresh client); removed server via `setServers` → watcher stopped (stub `close` called); `dispose` → all watchers closed. Static source check: `mcpManager.ts` imports `mcpDebugArgs`/`mcpWatchTarget` and `fs`. Gate **858 → 870** (+12).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** compile passes; smoke 870/870; a stdio server configured with `dev.debug: true` spawns with `--inspect` (node) or `-m debugpy --listen 5678` (python) and completes the normal handshake; a stdio server with `dev.watch: "<glob>"` restarts (close + re-handshake, status back to `running`) when a matching file changes and does NOT restart on non-matching changes; removing the server from config or disposing the manager stops all watchers (no leaked handles — `persistent: false` + explicit close); servers without `dev` and all HTTP servers behave exactly as before; no new deps.
- **Risks:** `fs.watch` is directory-level and platform-behavior varies (macOS FSEvents coalesces; Linux inotify is per-file but `fs.watch` on a dir reports child changes) — the 500 ms debounce + glob re-match keeps it correct at the cost of a small delay; a glob whose literal prefix does not exist yet → `fs.watch` throws → swallowed with a `notify` (documented: create the dir first); `dev.watch` on a `url` server is silently ignored (no process to restart) — documented; `debugpy` must already be installed in the Python environment (we only add launch args, never install) — documented; `--inspect` port 9229 / debugpy port 5678 are fixed defaults (no port config in this item — matches "keep it minimal"); concurrent watch-triggered restarts are serialized by the existing `starting` dedupe in `ensureStarted` (a restart while a start is in flight reuses the in-flight promise — acceptable); the watcher is per-manager (one `McpManager` instance in the extension) so no duplicate watchers per server.
- **Next item:** 1.101-6 · Chat UX improvements (distinct user messages, visible undo, navigable attachments).
